text:
alex: Proposal: trim default non-privileged auth/logins from 365d -> 60d to reduce storage and limit exposure. Keep privileged/audit trails longer. Plan includes short-lived forensic snapshots, strict RBAC, and a KMS proxy for unwraps. Thoughts?

mira: 60d is a bit aggressive. Any compliance hits? PCI/ISO/Tier-1 customers may want longer.

alex: talked to legal — for most internal product telemetry 60d is ok, but we need an exemption table + legal-hold path for customers with contractual obligations. Will capture exceptions in the RFC.

jin: How will this affect downstream SIEM consumers and historical analytics?

alex: SIEM ingest continues for realtime. For longer historical needs, we'll provide:
- aggregated metrics retained for 12 months in our metrics DB (no raw PII)
- on-demand snapshot exports of raw partitions (timeboxed, CMK-wrapped) for approved requests
- cold encrypted archive per-customer (CMK-bound) for full raw data if customer purchased extended retention

sam: RBAC: suggest two new ephemeral scopes: `log_snapshot_requester` (can create snapshot requests) and `log_snapshot_viewer` (can view snapshots for a bounded window). All grants must include expiry. Approvals require a SecOps approver or legal depending on scope.

katie: For KMS, we should avoid granting Decrypt to many identities. I'll prototype a KMS-unwrap proxy that issues ephemeral unwrap tokens bound to a snapshot id and justification. Example flow: 
```
# request unwrap token (requires approver)
curl -X POST https://kms-proxy.redwood/api/v1/unwrap-request \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"snapshot":"snap-auth-20260321-01","justification":"vuln-782","ttl":3600}'

# proxy returns: {"unwrap_token":"tkn_eyJ...","expires_at":"2026-03-21T10:15:00Z"}
```
Proxy then uses CMK to decrypt temporarily and returns unwrapped payload to caller with token. All unwraps are recorded.

mira: Audit trail is critical. We should log: principal, request_id, approver, justification, token_id, ip, query fingerprint, and result. Those audit records need a longer retention (3 years) separate from raw logs.

alex: OK - new audit stream `kms_unwrap_events` with 3y retention, immutable and forwarded to forensic bucket when a legal-hold exists.

jin: Will reducing raw retention break long-running trend detection (e.g., 9-12 month baselines)?

alex: We'll keep behavior baselines/aggregates for 12 months and export model features for long-term ML. Raw data older than 60d goes to cold archive (only for accounts with extended retention enabled). That keeps detection intact for most use cases.

sam: Emergency/legal-hold: implement a ticket that triggers a copy of affected partitions to `legal-hold` bucket with a separate CMK and 7y retention. The copy operation should be synchronous w/ proof-of-copy entry in audit log.

katie: Also recommend a tiny CLI + web flow for triage to reduce friction: `redwood sec snapshot create --dataset auth --window 2h --just "incident-#123"` which opens the approval workflow and returns snapshot_id.

opsbot: RFC draft created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/812 - contains lifecycle rules, RBAC matrix, and KMS-proxy sketch :paperclip:

mira: Please add approver matrix and SLOs (snapshot create latency goal < 5min, unwrap token issuance < 30s after approval). Also add who can escalate approvals during incidents.

alex: Will add matrix. Tentative RBAC approvers: SecOps leads or oncall for triage (<4h auto-approve window), Legal + Sec for customer legal-hold.

jin: For SIEM exports: enforce that any export copy is CMK-wrapped and TTL-limited (auto-delete after X days). Also surface export metadata to consumer so they can purge on their side.

alex: Good. We'll require export consumers to present a one-time-access token and an approved ticket id. Exports will have embedded expiry and be logged to `export_activity` stream (1y retention for metadata).

sam: I'll draft the RBAC policy changes tomorrow. I'll include example least-privilege IAM snippets and TTL enforcement.

katie: I'll build a POC of the kms-proxy and the demo CLI this week. Will post a link in the RFC.

mira: :thumbsup: keep me posted for legal-hold wording so legal can sign off.

alex: Thanks all. I'll update RFC with: 60d default, snapshot roles + timebound grants, kms-proxy + unwrap audit (3y), export gating + CMK-wrap, and legal-hold copy process (7y). Scheduling a 30m sync after RFC update.
